acceptance.requirement: The #1823 test owner freezes exact base, allowed test paths, acceptance mapping, expected red baseline, runtime probes, mutation controls and a self-consistent contract digest before implementation.

Exactly one editable issue-orchestration authoring package owns the Skill, runtime, policies, graph schemas, templates, installer and seven roles; target-repository copies, retired roles, aliases and fixed-Sol policy are absent.

The package manifest binds schema/version, source commit/tree, skill/agent/template artifacts, model pool, routing, stage permissions, remote mutation policy, graph/patch/runtime schemas, projector, caller-supplied repository admission, an empty source-repository dependency set, required capabilities, install targets and its own canonical digest.

Install, verify and uninstall are deterministic, atomic, external to the authoring checkout and all caller-supplied protected roots, and ownership-safe; unknown edits fail closed and no half install or unrelated deletion is allowed.
The current package root and four isolated temporary cwd probes discover the same skill identity/digest, exact seven-agent set and model/routing/remote-mutation/graph/projector digests.

The shared artifact carries stage-model-pool.v3 routing, root Luna/low, separated semantic graph/runtime projection, dispatch/self-test receipt authority and deterministic runtime modules without semantic compatibility fallback.
Semantic graph, ledger, runtime projection, receipts and resource state stay in a caller-supplied external runtime root and never enter authoring or installed artifacts.

The shared package owns only orchestration semantics and references each caller-supplied repository's AGENTS/current facts at runtime; it contains no fixed product identity, product allowlist, sibling-checkout dependency, or copied product design, API, documentation, or runtime authority.
Every acceptance gate is mapped to executable focused tests, real install/discovery/runtime probes and explicit negative mutation controls, with the old base recorded as red.
